headline: ICJ Ruling Opens a Further UN Route if Myanmar Does Not Comply
deck: The court called for reparations; if Myanmar does not perform the judgment, the other party may seek Security Council recourse.
body: International Court of Justice President Yuji Iwasawa said nine of the court’s 15 judges found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya [E1]. The court called for Myanmar to provide reparations and restitution [E3].
More than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya fled to Bangladesh during Myanmar’s 2016-17 military campaign [E2].

The UN Charter gives the other party in an ICJ case recourse to the Security Council if a party fails to perform a judgment; the Council may then make recommendations or decide measures [E4]. A negative vote from any permanent member prevents a substantive Council resolution or decision [E5].

**The desk's reading.** The finding establishes Myanmar’s responsibility and the court has called for reparations. If Myanmar does not perform, the other party may seek Security Council recourse; the Council may make recommendations or decide measures [E4]. The strongest competing reading is that Article 94 supplies a formal route but not a practical enforcement route, because a negative vote from any permanent member prevents a substantive Council decision [E5].

**The next test.** If a party alleges nonperformance and the Council adopts a substantive recommendation or measure, that would show the Charter channel can produce collective action [E4]. A negative vote by a permanent member that prevents such a decision would instead support the competing reading [E5].

evidence_box.fragment: The ICJ president, Yuji Iwasawa, said a majority of nine judges on the 15-seat court found that ‘the Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya’.

source_note.raw_excerpt: The ICJ president, Yuji Iwasawa, said a majority of nine judges on the 15-seat court found that ‘the Republic of the Union of Myanmar has committed genocide against the Rohingya’.

evidence_box.fragment: The 2016-17 campaign by Myanmar’s military forced more than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya to flee across the border into Bangladesh.

source_note.raw_excerpt: The 2016-17 campaign by Myanmar’s military forced more than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya to flee across the border into Bangladesh, arriving with reports of mass killings of adults and children, gang-rapes and burned-down villages.
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim text from the source page.

evidence_box.fragment: Iwasawa called for Myanmar to provide reparations and restitution.

source_note.raw_excerpt: During a reading of the decision that lasted more than two hours in a packed Great Hall of Justice in The Hague, Iwasawa called for Myanmar to provide reparations and restitution.
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim text from the source page.

evidence_box.fragment: If a party fails to perform an ICJ judgment, the other party may seek Security Council recourse, which may make recommendations or decide measures.

source_note.raw_excerpt: If any party to a case fails to perform the obligations incumbent upon it under a judgment rendered by the Court, the other party may have recourse to the Security Council, which may, if it deems necessary, make recommendations or decide upon measures to be taken to give effect to the judgment.

evidence_box.fragment: A negative vote by any permanent member prevents approval of a substantive Council resolution or decision.

source_note.raw_excerpt: It was agreed by the drafters that if any one of the five permanent members cast a negative vote in the 15-member Security Council, the resolution or decision would not be approved.
